items.title: Carpenter, Joiner & Cabinet Maker Roles in Adelaide
items.summary: Choose the right timber scope and agree the handovers between site carpentry, architectural joinery and cabinetry before comparing quotes.
items.content_html:
Buyer Guide

Carpenter, Joiner & Cabinet Maker Roles in Adelaide

Choose by the work and its interfaces: a carpenter handles site timber work, a joiner creates fitted timber details, and a cabinet maker focuses on cabinets and storage. The scope can overlap, so confirm each provider’s actual responsibilities.

Editorial guidance by MEL ONE

Carpenter, Joiner and Cabinet Maker Responsibilities

Site carpentry may involve framing, doors, trims or renovation timber work. Architectural joinery involves fitted features and detailed timber elements; cabinet making focuses on kitchens, wardrobes and other storage. These descriptions are a starting point, not proof of a provider’s capability. List the items you need and ask who will measure, manufacture, install and finish each one.

Ask for relevant work examples and a written description of the proposed scope. Confirm who contracts the work, who supervises it where required and how to check the relevant licence details. A workshop, a broad service list or a company registration alone does not establish authority for every type of building work.

For example, a new door opening and a fitted cabinet may share dimensions, but the quote should name who sets out the opening, who measures the finished space and who supplies each item.

Trade Handovers and Final Measurements

One contact can make communication simpler, but a combined quote does not establish that every trade is delivered by the same person. Ask which work is included, which specialists are separately engaged and who resolves the junctions. A clear allocation of responsibilities matters whether you appoint one provider or several.

A wall lined before a niche is measured, a benchtop ordered before services are set or a door that catches a cabinet can require finished work to be altered. Agree the relevant measurement and service positions before ordering the affected pieces.

Recheck critical dimensions after relevant linings, floor finishes and service positions are settled. Record any change from the drawing and name the person who approves it before workshop production begins. That hold point matters whether one provider or several trades deliver the work.

Comparing Quotes and the Work Sequence

When comparing quotes, look for who owns set-out, site measure, shop drawings, material selection, protection, installation, adjustments and handover. A low initial figure may exclude the coordination that makes a complex room fit together. A useful quote names assumptions and interfaces so the owner can see what must be resolved before work starts.

For a renovation or new build, the process normally moves from brief and drawings to site verification, detail decisions, production timing, staged installation and final adjustment. Not every project needs a large formal programme, but every project benefits from agreeing who makes decisions, when dimensions are confirmed and how late changes will be managed.

Team Selection and Scope Checks

Ask what work is completed in-house, who will be your site contact, how measurements are verified and when custom pieces are released for manufacture. Request the process for approving a changed dimension or material and for recording an installation defect. Those answers identify who makes each decision and how it reaches the site team.

Choosing a carpentry and joinery scope

Do I need one carpenter, joiner or cabinet maker for all the timber work?

No. The useful question is whether site dimensions, drawings, sequencing and responsibility are agreed. Separate providers can work together when their interfaces are documented.

Is a kitchen cabinet quote the same as a renovation quote?

No. A cabinetry quote can cover cabinet construction and installation while demolition, services, surfaces and making-good are separately agreed. Compare the included items before comparing totals.

When should final joinery measurements be taken?

At the stage when the relevant walls, floors, openings and service positions can be verified. Agree the measuring and drawing approval points before releasing custom pieces for manufacture.

How can I check a carpenter's licence in South Australia?

Use the Consumer and Business Services register to check the licence holder and relevant details, then confirm that the proposed work and contracting arrangements match. Company identity alone does not answer that question.

  • CBS: find a licence holder

Describe the timber items and handovers

List the timber items, rooms and other trades involved so MEL ONE can discuss who measures, makes and installs each part. Photos and drawings are optional for the first enquiry; email available files to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com. Final site measurements and agreed details are needed before manufacture or installation.

items.title: Kitchen Cabinetry Costs Adelaide — Comparing Quote Inclusions
items.summary: Understand the cabinetry choices, site work, allowances and exclusions that shape a kitchen quote, without relying on generic market price bands.
items.content_html:
Cost Guide

Kitchen Cabinetry Costs Adelaide — Comparing Quote Inclusions

A useful kitchen quote prices a defined scope. Compare cabinet layout, materials, hardware, installation and separate trade work before comparing the total.

We provide Kitchen & Bathroom Cabinetry — discuss your project with us.

Editorial guidance by MEL ONE

Comparing Kitchen Cabinetry Quotes for the Same Scope

A door refresh, replacement cabinets and a changed room layout are different projects. List what remains and what is removed, the number and arrangement of cabinets, drawers and panels, and the installation work required. A total without this detail cannot show whether two quotes cover the same outcome. There is no reliable project price until the scope and conditions are understood.

Cabinet size and complexity, substrate, visible finish, edging, drawer and hinge systems, internal accessories and appliance integration all affect the cabinetry scope. Transport, access, removal, protection and making-good also need an allocation. Benchtops, splashbacks, electrical and plumbing work should be identified as included, excluded or separately quoted rather than assumed to sit inside a cabinet total.

Cabinet depth, drawer configuration, appliance clearances, door style, handle detail and internal storage affect both cost and usability. Finish samples are important, but they should follow a layout that works. A client who understands the cabinet construction and hardware choices can compare alternatives more clearly than one choosing colour first and discovering functional compromises later.

A hypothetical comparison: one quote reuses sound boxes and changes doors, while another replaces all cabinets and includes new drawers. Compare those inclusions first; the totals alone do not price the same result.

Retaining the Layout and Existing Cabinet Boxes

Retaining a workable cabinet layout or sound cabinet boxes may reduce the work, but their condition and compatibility need checking. Compare simpler door details, a different finish or fewer specialist accessories against daily storage needs. Moving services needs a separately defined trade scope; it cannot be priced from a universal allowance or justified by a generic saving claim.

Keeping plumbing, waste and major electrical points can simplify a renovation, but it should not override a layout that fails the household. Start with the non-negotiables: cooking workflow, storage, access, appliance positions and circulation. Then identify which changes add genuine daily value and which are aesthetic moves that can be deferred or achieved another way.

Benchtop Decisions Before Cabinetry Ordering

Discuss the selected benchtop product with the responsible supplier and installer before specifying it. The engineered-stone prohibition and the distinction between new products and legacy work are explained in the sourced FAQ below. A material choice should be lawful, suitable for the room and coordinated with cabinet support and templating; it does not imply MEL ONE supplies or installs every benchtop system.

Trade Sequence and the Initial Kitchen Brief

A kitchen renovation often involves demolition, rough-in services, wall and floor preparation, cabinetry installation, benchtop templating, splashback work, appliance connection and final adjustment. The exact order depends on the project. Identifying who owns each handover helps prevent a finished cabinet being removed or altered because a service or surface was not ready.

Start with the kitchen location, what you want to retain, storage priorities, appliance models if selected, and any known access or occupancy limits. Existing photos, approximate dimensions and drawings are optional at first enquiry. The site measure and agreed specification turn that initial discussion into a defined cabinetry quote; unresolved selections should remain identifiable allowances or exclusions.

Kitchen cabinetry quote questions

Why can two kitchen cabinetry totals differ?

They may cover different cabinet quantities, finishes, hardware, removal, installation or making-good. Ask for those items and any allowances to be described so you can compare the same scope.

Can new engineered-stone benchtops be specified?

New engineered-stone benchtops, panels and slabs have been prohibited in South Australia since 1 July 2024. Legacy work and exemptions have separate conditions; this does not mean all stone products or all work on existing engineered stone are banned. Confirm the selected product and any existing-material work against current SafeWork SA guidance with the responsible specialist.

  • SafeWork SA: engineered-stone prohibition
Does a cabinet installation quote cover plumbing and electrical work?

Only when the written scope expressly includes the relevant arrangements. Identify the responsible trades, appliance connections, benchtops, splashbacks and surface preparation separately rather than assuming a complete kitchen renovation is included.

Can I start without a measured kitchen plan?

Yes. Describe the intended change and your storage priorities. Photos, approximate dimensions and drawings are optional for the first discussion; site measurement and agreed specifications are needed before a confirmed manufacturing scope.

Prepare a cabinetry quote brief

Describe the cabinets you want to retain or replace, storage priorities and selected appliances. MEL ONE can discuss cabinetry options and identify removal, installation and separate trade work in the quote. Photos, dimensions and drawings are optional initially; email available files to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com before arranging the site measure.

items.title: Heritage Timber Restoration Adelaide — Original Fabric and Retention
items.summary: Understand significance, retention and evidence when deciding how traditional timber work differs from ordinary renovation.
items.content_html:
Heritage Timber Guide

Heritage Timber Restoration Adelaide — Original Fabric and Retention

Start with what gives the timber significance and what can safely be retained. Heritage restoration balances condition, use and the evidence of original construction before choosing a repair or replacement.

We provide Heritage Carpentry — discuss your project with us.

Editorial guidance by MEL ONE

Heritage Status, Significance and Original Timber

Age or an architectural style alone does not establish heritage protection. Check the property’s status and discuss the proposed work through the relevant planning and heritage pathway before changing significant fabric. Approval requirements depend on the place and the work; there is no universal permit or mandatory adviser rule that can be inferred from a timber repair description. Official guidance is linked in the FAQ below.

Heritage timber work brings together the significance of existing fabric, its condition and the building’s present use. A visible original window may have heritage value even when it needs careful repair for weathering or operation. Retention can include targeted repairs; it need not mean leaving every defect untouched.

Original Profiles and Joinery Evidence for Repairs

Surviving profiles, joints, hardware and finish evidence help establish an appropriate detail. A traditional joint or particular species may be relevant, but the repair specification should follow the actual element and the agreed conservation approach. Do not assume every period building needs the same timber, connector or coating simply because its appearance is similar.

Profiles, surviving sections, old photographs, hardware and adjacent examples can all inform a repair or replacement detail. Recording these references before dismantling helps avoid a generic modern interpretation. Where a precise match is not possible, the proposed difference should be discussed openly with the project team and any relevant heritage adviser, not concealed by vague language.

For example, an adjacent intact sash may show a profile that a damaged window no longer reveals. Record it before removal, then agree whether the proposed detail should be repaired, replicated or referred for conservation advice.

Conservation Advice and Carpentry Responsibilities

MEL ONE can discuss heritage timber carpentry against the recorded condition and agreed project information. The relevant authority decides formal approvals; heritage advisers and other responsible specialists address their own scopes. Ask what assessment, drawings, specifications and authorisations the proposed work needs before appointing the repair work.

Structural concerns, active water entry, glazing, suspect coatings and other old materials may need separate assessment and specialist arrangements. Include those responsibilities in the project brief. A carpentry discussion does not establish engineering, hazardous-material or approval authority, and preparation should not disturb unknown materials merely to obtain a photograph.

Moisture Checks, Handover Records and Future Care

Timber does not fail in isolation. Flashing, drainage, glazing, paint, sealants, ventilation and adjacent masonry can all influence the service life of a repaired element. A restoration scope should identify these interfaces and the trades involved. This protects both the historic material that remains and the new timber introduced as part of a careful repair.

Keep photos, notes on retained and replaced elements, material or finish information, and a simple schedule for review. This record gives future owners or trades a clearer picture of what was repaired and why. Heritage stewardship is easier when maintenance is based on evidence rather than a cycle of reacting only after paint failure, water entry or decay becomes obvious.

Heritage conservation decision questions

Does heritage timber restoration rule out replacement of damaged pieces?

No. Retain sound significant material where appropriate, then compare local repair, replication or replacement against condition and the agreed conservation approach. Document the reason for each intervention.

Does an old Adelaide house automatically count as heritage listed or need approval?

No. Age alone does not establish heritage listing or the approval requirements. Check the property status and the proposed work. PlanSA explains how to find out whether approval is needed; the relevant authority determines the applicable requirements.

  • PlanSA: find out if you need approval
Where can I read about work in a State Heritage Area?

The South Australian environment department explains living and working in a State Heritage Area. Use that guidance to clarify the place and proposal with the relevant authority; do not assume the same pathway applies to every older property.

  • SA environment: living in a State Heritage Area
What should I read once the conservation approach is clear?

Use the practical heritage timber repair guide to prepare a condition record, identify elements and describe the proposed scope. Bring existing project advice to the discussion so the carpentry quote follows the agreed approach.

  • Prepare a heritage repair scope

Discuss the conservation approach

Describe the original timber you want to retain and any known heritage status or conservation advice. MEL ONE can discuss the recorded condition and proposed carpentry approach before a repair quote. Existing photos and advice are optional at first enquiry; email available files to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com.

items.title: Solid vs Engineered Timber Flooring Adelaide — Room and Restoration Choices
items.summary: Compare solid and engineered timber by product, subfloor, wear layer and maintenance, then decide what can be repaired or refinished.
items.content_html:
Material Guide

Solid vs Engineered Timber Flooring Adelaide — Room and Restoration Choices

Neither solid nor engineered timber is automatically the better floor. Compare the selected product with the subfloor, moisture conditions, room use and future maintenance before choosing replacement or restoration.

We provide Deck Restoration & Timber Floor Repairs — discuss your project with us.

Editorial guidance by MEL ONE

Condition Checks Before Timber Floor Restoration

Solid timber boards have timber through their thickness, but that does not promise an unlimited number of sandings or a fixed lifespan. Existing sanding, fixing position, damage, movement and the board profile affect what can be restored. Assess the actual floor before treating sanding and oiling as the solution; local repairs or a different finish approach may be needed.

Before selecting solid or engineered timber, understand slab or subfloor condition, flatness, moisture history, access, acoustic expectations and transitions to adjacent rooms. These factors affect preparation, installation method and long-term movement more than a showroom sample can reveal.

Solid and Engineered Timber Floors for the Room

Engineered flooring combines a timber surface with a layered construction. Products differ in wear-layer thickness, installation method, finish and repair options. Price and suitability cannot be expressed as one percentage of solid flooring. Check the manufacturer’s information and the existing floor before assuming it can be sanded or installed directly over a particular slab.

A ground-floor slab does not automatically make engineered timber suitable, and an upper floor does not automatically favour solid timber. Moisture assessment, subfloor preparation, acoustic requirements, floor height and the selected system need to agree. For rooms with frequent water exposure, confirm the product’s stated application limits before choosing any floor covering.

A sunny living room, upper-level bedroom, entry, apartment and renovation over an existing slab place different demands on timber flooring. Consider traffic, pets, direct light, furniture, cleaning habits and the desired feel underfoot. The most suitable product is the one whose visual character, maintenance needs and installation conditions all match the room’s real use.

Appearance, Movement and Floor-edge Details

Timber is a natural material and can show grain, tone and seasonal movement. Board direction, width, feature grade, finish sheen and transition details influence how that variation reads across a room. Discussing samples and laying patterns early helps clients choose a look they will value over time rather than expecting every board to be identical.

Flooring projects often become complicated at thresholds, fireplace surrounds, built-ins, stair nosings, skirtings and door clearances. These details deserve attention before the main field is installed. A clear plan for edges and transitions creates a more durable, finished result and prevents a small unresolved junction from holding up a larger room at the end.

Flooring Handover and Ongoing Care

The right cleaning method, furniture protection, prompt attention to spills and sensible use of mats can help preserve a timber floor. Care advice should match the selected product and finish, not rely on a generic rule. Ask what to avoid, how to treat minor wear and when a professional review is appropriate so maintenance becomes planned rather than reactive.

Solid and engineered flooring questions

Can an engineered timber floor be sanded?

Sometimes, but the remaining wear layer, previous sanding, damage and manufacturer’s requirements decide what is possible. Do not assume a standard number of refinishes applies to every engineered floor.

Is solid timber always more expensive?

No useful comparison follows from the material name alone. Compare the selected product, subfloor preparation, removal, installation, edges and finishing for the same room and scope.

Will oiling fix a damaged timber floor?

Oiling changes the surface finish; it does not resolve loose boards, moisture problems or deep damage. Assess the cause and condition before agreeing repairs and a compatible finish.

What belongs in a floor restoration quote?

Record the floor type if known, rooms, accessible condition, repair areas, preparation, finish, transitions, furniture handling and access. Separate concealed conditions and other trade work from the agreed floor scope.

Describe the existing floor before selecting a finish

Name the rooms, floor type if known, and any worn, loose or moving boards. MEL ONE can assess local repair, replacement and finishing options for the existing floor. Photos and approximate dimensions are optional initially; email them to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com if useful before the visit.

Before selecting solid or engineered timber, understand slab or subfloor condition, flatness, moisture history, access, acoustic expectations and transitions to adjacent rooms. These factors affect preparation, installation method and long-term movement more than a showroom sample can reveal.

Solid and Engineered Timber Floors for the Room

Engineered flooring combines a timber surface with a layered construction. Products differ in wear-layer thickness, installation method, finish and repair options. Price and suitability cannot be expressed as one percentage of solid flooring. Check the manufacturer’s information and the existing floor before assuming it can be sanded or installed directly over a particular slab.

A ground-floor slab does not automatically make engineered timber suitable, and an upper floor does not automatically favour solid timber. Moisture assessment, subfloor preparation, acoustic requirements, floor height and the selected system need to agree. For rooms with frequent water exposure, confirm the product’s stated application limits before choosing any floor covering.

A sunny living room, upper-level bedroom, entry, apartment and renovation over an existing slab place different demands on timber flooring. Consider traffic, pets, direct light, furniture, cleaning habits and the desired feel underfoot. The most suitable product is the one whose visual character, maintenance needs and installation conditions all match the room’s real use.

Appearance, Movement and Floor-edge Details

Timber is a natural material and can show grain, tone and seasonal movement. Board direction, width, feature grade, finish sheen and transition details influence how that variation reads across a room. Discussing samples and laying patterns early helps clients choose a look they will value over time rather than expecting every board to be identical.

Flooring projects often become complicated at thresholds, fireplace surrounds, built-ins, stair nosings, skirtings and door clearances. These details deserve attention before the main field is installed. A clear plan for edges and transitions creates a more durable, finished result and prevents a small unresolved junction from holding up a larger room at the end.

Flooring Handover and Ongoing Care

The right cleaning method, furniture protection, prompt attention to spills and sensible use of mats can help preserve a timber floor. Care advice should match the selected product and finish, not rely on a generic rule. Ask what to avoid, how to treat minor wear and when a professional review is appropriate so maintenance becomes planned rather than reactive.

Solid and engineered flooring questions

Can an engineered timber floor be sanded?

Sometimes, but the remaining wear layer, previous sanding, damage and manufacturer’s requirements decide what is possible. Do not assume a standard number of refinishes applies to every engineered floor.

Is solid timber always more expensive?

No useful comparison follows from the material name alone. Compare the selected product, subfloor preparation, removal, installation, edges and finishing for the same room and scope.

Will oiling fix a damaged timber floor?

Oiling changes the surface finish; it does not resolve loose boards, moisture problems or deep damage. Assess the cause and condition before agreeing repairs and a compatible finish.

What belongs in a floor restoration quote?

Record the floor type if known, rooms, accessible condition, repair areas, preparation, finish, transitions, furniture handling and access. Separate concealed conditions and other trade work from the agreed floor scope.

Describe the existing floor before selecting a finish

Name the rooms, floor type if known, and any worn, loose or moving boards. MEL ONE can assess local repair, replacement and finishing options for the existing floor. Photos and approximate dimensions are optional initially; email them to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com if useful before the visit.

Process Guide

Shop Fit Out Carpentry Adelaide — Scope and Installation Sequence

Plan a commercial carpentry fitout around decisions and site readiness, then agree a programme. Design, approvals, services, manufacturing and installation depend on each other; a generic week count cannot establish your opening date.

We provide Commercial Fitout & Refurbishment — discuss your project with us.

Editorial guidance by MEL ONE

Commercial Carpentry Fitout Scope

Identify counters, fitted storage, trims, partitions or feature joinery that belong in the timber package. Name the owner or authorised tenant contact, designer, head contractor and responsible specialists where involved. Agree who supplies the drawings, coordinates services and authorises changes; do not assume a carpentry contractor also owns the entire tenancy design or approval process.

Before fixing the fitout programme, confirm any lease or landlord requirements, existing services, base-building condition, access rules and approval pathway. Record whether deliveries can enter the site, whether proposed service routes are available and who obtains any required approval. If one of those points remains open, identify the affected joinery decision and allow for it in the programme rather than treating an intended opening date as a confirmed installation date.

Tell MEL ONE the premises, intended opening date, occupancy arrangements, timber items and nominated project contacts. Existing drawings, dimensions and photos are optional for the initial enquiry. A site assessment can clarify the accessible conditions and carpentry scope. Required decisions and authorisations must be resolved by the responsible parties before the affected work proceeds.

Site Readiness Before Manufacture and Installation

Review site dimensions, finished floor levels, service positions, materials and approved drawings before the affected pieces are manufactured. Record what must be ready for installation, who provides access and where materials can be stored. Production and installation timing depend on those decisions and supplier availability, so confirm the programme against the actual scope.

List unresolved approvals, selections, lead times, base-building preparation and service interfaces before fixing work dates. For an operating site, agree working areas, isolation, protection, deliveries and access arrangements. Ask who updates the programme when a dependency changes and how variations are authorised. Separate the desired opening date from the installation commitments actually agreed.

Layout, approvals, selected long-lead materials, service positions and core joinery dimensions can affect manufacture and following trades. Put a decision owner and due date against each of these dependencies. Movable furniture and minor decorative items may be decided later if they do not alter fixed joinery, access or services; check that assumption against the actual scope.

For a hypothetical counter, a change to service positions after final measurement can affect its cut-outs and installation date. Record who signs off the dimensions and who releases the joinery for manufacture.

Specialist Services and Quality Checks

Counters, ceilings, partitions and feature walls commonly meet power, data, mechanical, hydraulic and fire services. The fitout team needs a shared view of where those interfaces occur and when they are checked. This is why shop drawings, site dimensions and trade coordination matter: they turn a visual layout into a buildable one without last-minute cutting into finished work.

Before a counter or partition is closed in, check the agreed dimensions, service openings and access for later trade work. Before handover, review visible finishes, operation, protection removal and outstanding adjustments against the written scope. Record who accepts each stage and who handles an unresolved item so it is addressed while the relevant trade can still reach it.

Commercial Carpentry Handover Records

Check the installed timber work against approved drawings and the agreed scope, operate doors and drawers, record adjustments and supply selected product care information. The tenant, head contractor and responsible specialists still need to coordinate their own completion and opening requirements. A carpentry handover alone does not establish permission to open the premises.

Commercial carpentry fitout questions

How long does a commercial carpentry fitout take?

The programme depends on scope, drawings, site readiness, selected materials, access and other trades. Agree the measuring, drawing approval, production and installation milestones for your project rather than relying on a universal duration.

Can I book commercial carpentry fitout work around shop opening hours?

Discuss the operating hours, protected routes, noise restrictions, deliveries and areas that can be released. Whether staging is workable depends on the premises and the agreed project arrangements.

Who handles fitout approvals and specialist services?

Name the responsible parties in the project scope. Carpentry does not automatically include design, fire, electrical, plumbing or approval services. Check the proposed work through the relevant approval pathway before relying on a programme.

  • PlanSA: find out if you need approval
What should be recorded at carpentry handover?

Record completed items, agreed adjustments, approved changes, hardware operation and care information. Keep any remaining specialist or opening requirements with their responsible parties.

Define the commercial timber package

List the counters, storage or other timber items, the premises' operating hours and the person coordinating the fitout. MEL ONE can discuss staging and the decisions needed before final measurement and manufacture. Drawings and photos are optional at first enquiry; email available files to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com.

Carpentry Planning Guide

Carpentry Costs Adelaide — Quote Comparison Guide

This is a quote-comparison guide, not a price list: MEL ONE rates and project prices are not published here. Compare the timber work, materials, access and allowances behind each total before accepting a carpentry quote.

Editorial guidance by MEL ONE

Defined Carpentry Jobs, Fixed Quotes and Hourly Rates

A carpenter hourly rate describes labour time rather than the total cost of a repair. Adjusting a sticking door, replacing deck boards and repairing concealed framing involve different materials, access and uncertainty. Define the item, quantity and intended result first, then ask how the proposed pricing arrangement covers that work.

A fixed quote and hourly arrangement answer different questions. A quoted amount needs a defined scope, quantities, inclusions, exclusions and stated assumptions. For hourly work, ask how time is recorded, which activities are chargeable and how progress and further authorisation will be discussed. Clarify whether procurement, travel, setup and return visits form part of that time or are separate items. Neither arrangement removes uncertainty in hidden timber. Agree how investigation and any later repair will be priced rather than assuming every job can receive an unconditional fixed price before assessment.

Photo Estimates, Measurements and Opening-up

Photos help describe a concern, but a close view of a rotten sill may omit the adjoining frame, water source or removal access. An initial estimate should state those assumptions and the inspection needed before a confirmed quote. Record accessible areas and any included opening-up work so concealed timber remains an explicit question.

The guide photo shows a tape measure across exposed, deteriorated deck timber. It records visible dimensions, but cannot establish which boards or supports can remain. Keep any safely available photos with the written scope, distinguish board repairs from frame repairs and agree investigation limits before more timber is opened up.

Opening a board, lining or joint can expose decay beyond the visible patch. That discovery can change the quantity of timber, connection details and specialist input needed. Ask how findings will be documented and which part of the original scope can proceed. MEL ONE confirms proposed scope changes and pricing for your approval before additional work proceeds. Record the agreed variation and any effect on timing. Where the damage affects load-bearing timber, resolve the required assessment and design responsibilities before treating it as a routine cosmetic repair.

Discuss deck repair and restoration scope · Discuss timber beneath the deck or floor

Materials, Access and Finishing Allowances

A carpentry quote in Adelaide should identify the elements to be repaired or supplied, with quantities or dimensions where practical. Describe the material, profile, grade or product selection rather than writing only 'new timber'. Confirm who orders, transports and stores it, and whether fittings, fasteners, protective coatings and delivery are included. Where you supply materials, discuss suitability, quantity and readiness before booking installation. Ask how unavailable products or requested substitutions will be handled. A material allowance needs a clear basis so a later selection can be compared with what was originally priced.

Work above a verandah, beneath a floor or around occupied rooms may need different access and protection arrangements. Identify restricted parking, stairs, working height, furniture, business hours and any coordination with other trades. Separate removal of old components from disposal, waste transport and final cleaning. State whether painting, staining, sealing, making good and adjoining surfaces are included, excluded or handled by another trade. For fascia, eaves or weatherboards, clarify the interfaces with gutters and surrounding materials. These details explain scope differences that a single total or hourly rate leaves hidden.

This hypothetical comparison contrasts selected-board replacement with a larger area lifted for joist inspection. They cover different work, so their totals cannot be compared until the board quantities and frame investigation are aligned. Ask both providers to identify retained components and unresolved findings against the same brief.

Checks Before Accepting a Written Quote

Read the quote as a complete document: agreed work, exclusions, allowances, GST treatment, payment stages, quote validity and proposed timing should be clear. Ask whether assessment, travel or a minimum booking charge applies; this guide does not assume those items are free or specify amounts. Note the acceptance process and who can approve changes, especially for rental or shared property. Send questions together so the revised written scope answers them before work starts. Keep the accepted quote and approved variations available for the final handover and account discussion.

Carpentry rates and quote questions

Can a photo of exposed deck timber establish the repair price?

It can help describe visible deterioration and the area being measured, but it cannot confirm the condition of concealed timber or the complete repair scope. Ask for an assessment that distinguishes board replacement from work to the supporting frame. Agree any opening-up allowance, document the findings and approve scope and price changes before additional work proceeds.

  • Deck repair and restoration planning
How much does a carpenter charge in Adelaide?

The amount depends on the agreed task, condition, access, materials and pricing arrangement. MEL ONE assesses the work and provides a written scope and price. Ask whether the quote is fixed or estimated and whether assessment, travel or minimum booking charges apply before accepting.

  • Discuss your carpentry scope
Does a carpentry quote include materials, rubbish removal, paint and GST?

Read the stated inclusions and exclusions. Ask for materials and procurement, removal and disposal, finishing and GST treatment to be explicit. If one item is absent or unclear, have the written scope clarified before accepting; do not assume that the total includes every stage.

  • Fascia and eaves repair planning
  • Weatherboard repair scope
Why might the price change after an inspection or opening up timber?

An inspection may reveal access constraints, different materials or deterioration that photos could not show. Opening up can expose further damaged members or connections. Distinguish an initial estimate from the agreed quote, document findings and confirm changes and pricing for approval before additional work proceeds.

  • Timber restoration and maintenance
  • Subfloor timber repairs
  • Framing scope and design interfaces
How can I compare two deck repair quotes that cover different work?

Create one brief and compare quantities, materials, retained framing, inspection allowances, labour, procurement, access, removal, waste, finish and GST. Check payment terms, validity and variation approval as well. Ask each provider to explain differences before deciding; totals alone do not show whether the same result is included.

  • Deck repair and restoration
  • New outdoor timber projects
  • Access and threshold carpentry planning

Send the timber task or repair list, location and access limits. MEL ONE can arrange a visit and price the defined work, with investigation and finishing allowances identified. Outdoor Materials Guide

Decking Material Advice Adelaide — Exposure, Timber and Maintenance

Useful decking material advice in Adelaide starts with how the site is exposed and how the space will be used. A colour sample is one decision; the supporting structure, fixing system and maintenance plan need attention too.

We provide Decks, Pergolas & Timber Screens — discuss your project with us.

Editorial guidance by MEL ONE

Site Exposure and Outdoor Timber Material Selection

Record which parts receive direct sun, stay shaded, collect leaves or remain wet after rain. Note whether sea air reaches the deck or the work is sheltered behind another building. Include irrigation, nearby planting, ground levels and water flowing from roofs or paving. Timber selection needs these site details rather than a suburb name alone. On an exposed coastal deck, record corroded fixings and their locations for assessment. Replacing visible boards does not establish the condition of the frame beneath them.

The guide photo shows a deck, steps and pergola together. Treat boards, supports, stair components and overhead members as separate material decisions: their exposure and structural roles differ. Appearance cannot identify species, treatment or concealed connections. Keep the agreed product, fixing and finish specifications with each component's care instructions.

Provide the property address and describe whether the proposal changes the structure, footprint, height or use of the outdoor area. Ask the relevant authority or responsible professional to assess applicable planning, building, heritage or bushfire-related requirements before final selection. For a proposed deck at an Adelaide Hills property, treat address-specific constraints as an early assessment question; a regional label does not determine a product's suitability. Where a ramp or threshold is involved, bring the user's access needs into the design discussion as well. This guide does not determine approval or compliance for a property.

Plan the separate elements of an outdoor timber project · Discuss pergola repair scope · Discuss timber steps, stairs and handrails

Timber and Composite System Specifications

Compare the exact proposed products, their appearance, maintenance instructions and installation requirements. A preference for solid timber or composite does not establish that either can simply replace existing boards on the same supports. Ask the supplier or manufacturer to confirm the proposed supporting arrangement, fixing method and movement provisions for the selected product. ModWood publishes product installation and technical documents, illustrating why a composite board should be considered with its specified system. Product references are planning resources, not a claim that MEL ONE has installed or endorses that product.

Ask the proposed supplier to identify the timber species or product name, dimensions, grade, treatment where relevant and intended use. Keep the board surface separate from the structural timber specification. Request supporting product information and flag any gaps for review by the responsible designer or supplier. Compare samples for appearance and surface feel, but record what the order actually includes: profiles, edge details, colour selection and any coating. Avoid choosing solely from a species name or a general 'outdoor suitable' description. The brief should make substitutions visible before materials are purchased.

Drainage, Ventilation, Framing and Fixings

WoodSolutions' domestic deck guidance identifies drainage and ventilation as design considerations. Raise questions about water leaving the surface, air moving beneath the deck and access for inspection. Proposed edge screens, landscaping and storage beneath the boards should be included in that discussion. Ask the designer to resolve ground clearance, board spacing and interfaces using the selected system's requirements. These details are especially useful when comparing a raised deck with a constrained, low-level area. A decorative finish cannot stand in for a workable drainage and ventilation arrangement.

For exposed coastal timber work, WoodSolutions' guidance gives particular attention to fixing selection. Ask which fasteners and connectors are proposed for the actual exposure, timber and supporting material, and what documentation supports that choice. Identify mixed metals, existing corrosion and concealed connections as assessment questions. Board screws, clips, joist connections and post connections have different roles; replacing one visible fixing does not confirm the others are suitable. Record who will assess retained supports and resolve any required structural details before agreeing to a surface-only replacement.

Finish and Maintenance in the Written Scope

Decide how you want the surface to look and what upkeep you can accommodate. items.summary: A practical deck replacement guide: how to distinguish surface wear from structural issues, what to inspect before requesting a quote, and how to scope a safer long-term repair.
items.content_html:
Decking Guide · 2026-09-23

Deck Replacement Adelaide — Repair and Replacement Decisions

Surface wear can suit restoration, while decay, movement or damaged connections call for assessment before deciding on repair or replacement. Keep people away from an area that appears unsafe and describe the symptoms to the assessor.

We provide Deck Restoration & Timber Floor Repairs — discuss your project with us.

Editorial guidance by MEL ONE

Deck Repair and Replacement Decisions

Faded colour, raised grain and worn finish do not by themselves establish that the deck frame needs replacing. Movement, soft timber, loose connections or a damaged stair or balustrade need an assessment of the affected construction. Record what you can see safely from normal access; do not remove boards, load-test the deck or disturb supports to investigate it yourself.

MEL ONE inspects the deck boards, frame, post bases and connections on site to identify the repair required. We explain whether selective board replacement or a wider repair suits the condition, discuss approvals and engineering requirements, and confirm the work scope and quote before structural changes begin.

The assessor needs to consider the accessible supports, framing, connections and moisture paths, not only the visible walking surface. Limited access may leave some conditions unresolved until an agreed investigation stage. The quote should identify those limits and explain how any newly exposed damage will be recorded and authorised before further work proceeds.

Exposure and Board Choices After Frame Assessment

Sun, rain and coastal air do not affect every Adelaide deck in the same way. An exposed western deck may need a different finishing cycle from a sheltered courtyard, while salt-laden air can accelerate corrosion where the wrong fixings have been used. The useful starting point is not a generic lifespan claim: note the deck orientation, shade, moisture paths, proximity to the coast and whether leaf litter or planter boxes keep sections damp.

Once the existing construction is understood, the replacement decision can be specific: retain sound framing, replace damaged members, choose a board profile, resolve edge details and confirm how stairs or balustrades meet the new work. Comparing options against exposure, maintenance preference and intended use is more useful than selecting timber only by colour.

Deck Repair Shortcuts and Adjoining Elements

Covering decayed timber, tightening a loose board without finding the cause, or applying a fresh coating to a damp surface may improve appearance briefly without solving the condition below. A transparent scope identifies unknown areas, access limitations and the sequence for opening or repairing them, so the client can make an informed decision about risk and budget.

Deck replacement often touches more than boards. Stairs, privacy screens, roof posts, planters, lighting, pools and external doors can affect the workable sequence. Mapping these interfaces before demolition helps preserve access and avoids a new deck being held up by an overlooked connection, service or finish that belongs to another part of the project.

For example, replacing boards beside a loose stair without defining the stair work leaves a different scope from a quote that includes both. Ask which accessible supports and adjacent items were assessed.

Deck Quote Inclusions and Handover

Tell MEL ONE the deck location, preferred material, access constraints and whether you want the existing frame checked for reuse. Existing wide photos, close-ups and plans are optional; email them to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com if available. We inspect the frame, measure the deck and check stairs, balustrades, seating and posts. The quote separates demolition, structural repairs, boards, stairs, handrails, finishing and waste removal, with any site-dependent items explained.

Keep the retained and replaced member record, finish details and care instructions at handover. Ask which drainage and connection areas need periodic review and how to report a concern. Photos taken before boards cover the frame can help a future repair team identify the work.

Deck repair or replacement questions

How do I know whether a deck needs repair or replacement?

Surface wear can be different from deterioration in boards, supports or connections. An assessment of the accessible boards, frame and connections establishes whether maintenance, local replacement or a wider scope suits the condition. Faded colour alone does not establish that the deck needs replacement.

Can my old deck frame be reused when replacing the boards?

Only after the frame and relevant connections have been assessed for the proposed work. Reuse should be an explicit scope decision with any inaccessible or concealed areas recorded.

What changes the deck repair quote?

The repair extent, access, retained framing, board selection, stairs, balustrades, finishing and waste handling all matter. Record hidden-condition allowances and specialist interfaces separately.

Where do I start if I want a completely new deck?

Use outdoor living carpentry for a new layout or new deck scope. Use deck restoration for an existing deck repair; changes to the design may require a separate approval and engineering discussion.

Photos and plans are optional for the first enquiry; email available files to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com without disturbing unsafe timber.

items.content_html:
Joinery Guide · 2026-09-23

Custom Wardrobe Planning Adelaide — Measurements, Layout and Quotes

MEL ONE turns your Adelaide custom wardrobe brief into a measured layout, an agreed materials and hardware specification, and a clear installation quote. Start with how you use the space, then confirm the site details before manufacture.

We provide Built-in Wardrobes & Custom Storage — discuss your project with us.

Editorial guidance by MEL ONE

Wardrobe Measurements and Usable Clearances

Overall width, height and depth are only the first layer. Note skirtings, cornices, power points, windows, light switches, return walls and door swings, plus any variation in floor or wall level. In older Adelaide homes, walls and ceilings are not always square; an on-site measure before manufacture is the point at which the cabinet dimensions, filler panels and scribe details can be finalised.

The internal depth, drawer projection, hanging clearance and shelf spacing must work with the garments and room, not just fit a nominal cabinet size. A wardrobe can lose useful capacity when a door, bed or window restricts access. Discussing these constraints early allows the layout to favour the items used daily and reserve higher or deeper areas for occasional storage.

Filler panels, scribes and small shadow lines are often the practical way for cabinetry to meet existing walls that are not straight. They should be treated as considered details, not defects. Reviewing samples, handle positions and the intended reveal between doors gives everyone a shared expectation before a custom wardrobe is manufactured and installed.

Internal Layout for Daily and Future Storage

List what the wardrobe must hold before selecting finishes. Long-hang clothing, folded garments, shoes, linen, bags, drawers and seasonal storage each need different clearances. Mix dedicated hanging zones with adjustable shelves and removable rails where future needs may change, such as a child growing or a room becoming a study. Size drawers for the items they will hold, and avoid deep, unlit shelves that become dead space rather than adding every available accessory.

A hypothetical bedroom brief might put long hanging space on one side and adjustable shelves on the other. Check the actual garments, drawer opening and room circulation before agreeing that arrangement.

Wardrobe Doors, Materials, Lighting and Ventilation

Hinged doors need clear swing space; sliding doors preserve circulation but limit access to part of the interior at once. Mirrored, painted and timber-look finishes each change light, maintenance and the visual weight of the room. For wardrobes near bathrooms, laundries or external walls, discuss moisture exposure and ventilation so the substrate, edging and installation detail suit the location.

Integrated lighting, power points and ventilation can make a wardrobe easier to use, but they need to be planned before the unit is built. Identify what requires electrical coordination, where cables or drivers can be accessed and whether exterior walls or adjoining wet areas create condensation concerns. These interfaces are resolved with the appropriate trades rather than retrofitted blindly.

Access, Site Measure and the Manufacturing Brief

Confirm access from the street to the room, stair turns, parking, flooring protection and the timing of painting, electrical work and new carpet. A clear installation sequence reduces the risk that joinery is measured before adjoining finishes are ready. To request a quote, tell MEL ONE what the wardrobe needs to store and the finishes you prefer. Existing room photos, a rough sketch and approximate measurements are optional; email them to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com if available. MEL ONE confirms the room and access measurements on site.

Use the site measurements to check walls, floors and access against the proposed internal layout. Review door movement, drawer projection, hardware clearances, filler details and any lighting interfaces together. Approve the drawings and specification before the final quoted scope proceeds to manufacture and installation.

Wardrobe Quote Inclusions and Approved Changes

The quote should describe the wardrobe location, layout and quantities: hanging zones, shelves, drawers and any selected accessories. Identify the cabinet substrate, edging, visible finishes, door material, handles and hardware. Confirm whether removal of an existing unit, transport, floor and room protection, waste removal, installation, wall or trim making-good, and lighting interfaces are included. Record exclusions and responsibilities clearly so the total scope is easy to compare.

An early budget estimate uses the information and selections available at that stage. A confirmed quote follows the site measure and agreed layout, materials, hardware and installation conditions. Where something still needs checking, record the assumption and how it will be resolved. Ask MEL ONE to explain the pricing basis and included costs rather than treating a photo-based estimate as an approved manufacturing specification.

Adding drawers, changing hinged doors to sliding doors or selecting a different door material can change hardware, internal access, fabrication and installation work. MEL ONE records the revised layout or specification and explains the effect on price and scheduling in a written variation. Approve that change before the affected work proceeds; keep the approved version alongside the original quote.

Wardrobe Handover Checks and Records

At handover, compare the installed layout and visible finish with the approved scope and final specification. Operate the doors and drawers; check handles, shelving, alignment, visible edges, agreed lighting access and how the unit meets the floor, walls and ceiling. Record any adjustment or outstanding work while the installation team is available, and keep the specification and surface-care information with the completion record.

Custom wardrobe planning questions

What measurements are needed for a wardrobe quote, and are photos enough?

For planning, note the available width, height and depth, ceiling slopes, skirtings, door swings and other obstructions if you already have that information. Photos and approximate measurements are optional for the first enquiry and can help MEL ONE discuss an initial budget. Room photos alone do not establish the final manufacturing dimensions or price. The confirmed quote follows the site measure, agreed design and specification, and installation arrangements.

What happens if I add drawers or change the doors?

We revise the layout, materials and hardware requirements, explain the effect on price and scheduling, and obtain approval for a written variation before the affected work proceeds.

Does the wardrobe quote include removal and making-good?

Check the written scope. Removal, transport, protection, waste, installation and making-good should each be listed as included, excluded or separately agreed.

What should I keep after installation?

Keep the approved design and specification, quote and variations, care information, and handover record showing completed work and any agreed follow-up.

Prepare your wardrobe brief

List the clothes and other items to store, available room space and your door preference. MEL ONE can develop the internal layout, then verify dimensions and agree materials, hardware and drawings before manufacture. Room photos and rough measurements are optional initially; email them to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com if available.

Heritage Timber Repairs Adelaide — Condition Records and Repair Scope

Prepare a condition record before deciding the repair scope: identify each element, describe visible symptoms and note access and existing project advice. This practical brief follows the conservation principles explained in the companion heritage guide.

We provide Heritage Carpentry — discuss your project with us.

Editorial guidance by MEL ONE

Element Records Before Heritage Timber Repairs

Use a room, elevation or simple element name such as front window or side door so everyone discusses the same item. Note sticking, visible decay, water entry, damaged profiles or missing hardware from safe normal access. Existing photos are optional for the first enquiry; do not disturb coatings, glazing or timber to make a record. The site assessment provides the accessible condition detail needed to develop the scope.

Old hardware, profiles, glazing bars, joints and paint layers can help explain how an element was built and what makes it visually significant. Recording those details before removal creates a better basis for repair or replication. It also allows owners, designers and heritage advisers to discuss a proposed change using evidence rather than a guess based on a modern equivalent.

Note when water entry occurs, which areas remain damp and any previous repairs. Accessible observations help the assessment, but hidden drainage, flashing, glazing or wall problems may need another specialist. Ask who investigates the cause and what must be resolved before the timber repair is finished; replacement timber alone does not establish that water entry has been fixed.

Retained Fabric, Concealed Decay and Quote Allowances

Ask the proposed scope to identify retained material, local repairs, replicated components or replacement items and the evidence behind each decision. Include profile references, finish responsibilities and unresolved conditions. The method must suit the assessed element and agreed conservation approach; a photo or generic repair description is not a specification for cutting or rebuilding old timber.

External joinery can conceal deterioration behind paint, trims or internal linings. MEL ONE checks the accessible timber on site and agrees any careful opening-up needed to identify the damage. If hidden decay is found, we explain the additional repair and agree the scope and quote with you before proceeding.

Approvals, Glazing, Paint and Staged Work

Include any known listing status, previous advice, approved drawings and relevant correspondence with the project record. Requirements depend on the place and proposal; use PlanSA guidance to start the approval check and ask the relevant authority about unresolved requirements. MEL ONE’s carpentry scope should follow the agreed project information rather than promise the authority’s decision.

A repaired timber window or door depends on more than its joinery. Glazing, putty or sealant, hardware adjustment, paint preparation and final coating need to follow an appropriate sequence. Clarifying those interfaces early prevents a repaired sash or door from being installed without the finishing work required to protect it from weather and daily use.

For several affected openings, agree which need attention first and which can wait. Keep the element records and agreed repair approach together so later stages use the same profile references, approval information and finishing details.

Maintenance Records After Timber Repair

Timber lasts longer when paint failure, failed sealant, blocked drainage paths and exposed end grain are addressed early. At handover, ask what has been repaired, which finish system has been used, when it should be reviewed and which warning signs—such as cracking, sticking, water entry or soft timber—should prompt another inspection.

What should a heritage timber condition record contain?

Identify each door, window or external element, the visible symptoms, access limits and any existing conservation or approval advice. Photos and approximate dimensions are optional at first enquiry; the assessment develops the repair scope.

How should hidden decay be handled in the quote?

Record what can be assessed, what remains concealed and any agreed investigation stage. Additional damage should be documented with its scope and price effect agreed before the affected repair proceeds.

Who checks approval requirements for a proposed repair?

Confirm the property status and proposed work with the relevant authority. Include known approval documents and name the person responsible for unresolved checks in the project brief.

items.content_html:
Framing Carpenter Adelaide — House Framing

MEL ONE installs timber wall, roof and floor framing to the project drawings. Member sizes, bracing and connections follow the coordinated design, with inspections arranged before the structure is covered.

Request a house framing quote0403 202 949

Stud Wall Framing: New Frames and Altered Walls

House framing establishes the timber structure before linings and finishes conceal it. For new stud wall framing, MEL ONE works from the issued layout, member sizes and connection details; for an altered wall, the existing construction and proposed change need review first. An opening for a door or window affects more than its visible width, so the brief should identify the full opening and its relationship to adjoining framing.

A renovation that exposes damaged studs needs a repair decision before the wall is closed again. Record the accessible damage, what supports the wall and which members are proposed for retention or replacement. Load-bearing alterations and repairs remain conditional on the responsible professional assessment, design and required project arrangements; a carpentry visit alone does not settle those questions.

Coordinate framing within a renovation

Roof Trusses, Rafters and Floor Joist Interfaces

Roof and floor framing must connect to the wall system described in the project documentation. Truss layouts, bearing points, rafters, floor joists and their connections need consistent information so one trade does not build an assumption into the next trade's work. A change to an opening, wall position or roof geometry should be referred back to the responsible designer before affected members are ordered or altered.

Discuss lifting access, delivery space and the route for long members early, especially on constrained renovation sites. The framing package should identify the timber and connections included and where supplier, builder and engineering responsibilities begin. Roof coverings, weatherproofing and service installation are separate interfaces to coordinate with the relevant trades.

Current Drawings, Set-out and Framing Materials

Architectural plans describe the spaces, while structural and supplier details establish member sizes, supports and connections for the affected work. Check that the drawing revisions agree before setting out wall lines, opening dimensions, stair voids and service allowances. Unresolved dimensions or conflicting details need an answer from the responsible project party before installation.

Timber selection follows the specified member, treatment and exposure, rather than substituting a similar-looking piece. Agree who orders and supplies timber, proprietary connections and trusses, and how deliveries will be stored and protected on site. Keeping material schedules with the current drawings makes it easier to identify a supply omission or changed detail before it disrupts the framing sequence.

Framing Sequence, Checks and Trade Handover

Installation needs an agreed order for wall frames, bracing, roof members and any floor system, with access and temporary stability considered throughout. Set practical hold points for project inspections while connections and bracing remain visible. If a revised detail affects installed work, agree how it will be addressed before another trade covers it.

MEL ONE's carpentry review covers accessible alignment, openings, connections, bracing and obvious damage within the agreed work. Those trade checks do not replace required building inspections or engineering sign-off. Record outstanding items, inspection responsibilities and what is ready for roof, cladding or internal trades at handover.

House Framing Quote Inclusions

A useful framing quote names the drawing revision, areas or members included and whether the allowance is labour-only or supply and installation. Separate lifting, site access, temporary support, connections to existing work and any removal or reinstatement. These differences can explain why two prices for the same floor plan cover different work.

Keep the quoted drawing revision with approved changes. Revised openings or concealed damage can alter labour and materials; agree the added work and price before installation. At handover, record completed framing, inspection status and outstanding items for the next trade.

Framing Plans, Inspections and Quote Questions

Can framing start from architectural drawings alone?

Architectural plans may leave member sizes, bracing or connections unresolved. Structural details and truss or supplier information need coordination with the responsible designer or engineer. Use matching drawing revisions and resolve missing details before the affected framing starts.

Who checks the frame before it is covered?

Agree the required inspections and the responsible builder, engineer or certifier in advance. MEL ONE's carpentry checks do not replace statutory inspections or engineering sign-off.

What changes a framing quote?

Compare quotes against the same drawing revision and member schedule. Supply versus labour-only work, trusses, connections, bracing, lifting access, temporary support and ties into existing construction can change the allowance. Ask which inspections and other project responsibilities remain separate and how revised drawings or concealed damage will be priced before extra work proceeds.

Outdoor Carpentry Adelaide — Decks, Pergolas & Timber Screens

New outdoor carpentry should suit how you use the yard and how it meets the house. MEL ONE discusses decking and pergola scope, material choices, access and the design responsibilities before work is scheduled.

Request a deck, pergola or screen quote0403 202 949

New Timber Decks: Levels, Drainage and Everyday Use

A new deck begins with how the yard meets the home: the door threshold, ground levels, circulation and the space needed for furniture. On a sloping backyard, a deck near the rear door can involve a very different supporting structure from a low garden platform. MEL ONE reviews the site and proposed use before the decking appearance becomes the main decision.

Plan drainage paths, ventilation beneath the boards and access to adjoining services with the deck layout. The agreed design determines supports, connections and transitions to paving or lawn. For an existing deck with split boards, peeling finish or movement, begin with a condition assessment through the deck restoration service; keeping an old frame is a decision to verify, not an automatic saving.

Assess an existing deck before replacement

Timber or Composite Decking: Compare the Complete System

Compare actual boards for appearance, surface feel, cleaning, coating requirements and future replacement. Timber species and composite products vary, so a material label alone does not establish lifespan, slip performance or a maintenance saving. The chosen fixing system and the product's installation requirements also affect the complete price.

Exposure, drainage, board spacing and the supporting frame need to suit the specified system. Ask how the selected finish will be cared for, which faces or cut ends need protection and whether replacement boards are available. For a pool edge or another special setting, identify the intended use so the relevant design and performance questions are resolved before ordering.

Compare decking material and exposure decisions

Timber Pergolas: Shade, Coverings and House Connections

Explain whether the aim is filtered shade, shelter from rain or an open garden structure. Those outcomes can require different details, and a timber pergola frame alone does not establish a weatherproof roof. Proposed coverings, shade equipment and other loads need to be identified before posts, beams and connections are selected.

A freestanding timber pergola and an attached structure also have different support and connection questions. An existing wall must be assessed for the proposed attachment; its convenient position does not show it can carry the load. Agree the responsible design and approval checks, and separate roof coverings, flashing, electrical work and weatherproofing from the timber package.

Repair existing pergola timber

Courtyard Privacy Screening: Sightlines, Battens and Supports

Privacy screening works best when the brief identifies the view to interrupt, the desired openness and the way people move through the courtyard. A closely spaced screen may change light and airflow as well as privacy. Compare batten direction, gaps, height and finish in the actual setting before confirming the layout.

Posts and fixing points need consideration alongside the appearance, particularly where a screen meets a fence, wall or deck. A decorative screen is not automatically a wind barrier, safety barrier or pool barrier. Boundary arrangements and any required design input should be resolved for the proposed location rather than assumed from a reference image.

Comparing Deck, Pergola and Screen Quotes

Compare each quote against the same layout, materials and supporting work. Identify site preparation, foundations or supports, board or batten quantities, fixings, delivery, removal, surface protection and finishing. A quote for a timber frame should clearly say which coverings and adjoining trades remain separately arranged.

Access for long timber, support construction and removal can affect the price as much as visible boards or battens. Compare those allowances with the selected layout and materials. At handover, review the finished junctions and keep material-care information with any outstanding roofing or other trade work.

Decking Materials, Pergola Connections and Maintenance Questions

Should I choose timber or composite boards for a new deck?

Compare actual products against the site, desired appearance, cleaning and maintenance requirements, fixing system and future repairs. Neither timber nor composite is suitable simply because of its label. The selected board, frame and drainage details need to work together under the project design and manufacturer requirements.

  • Repair or replace an existing deck
Can a pergola be attached to any existing wall?

An existing wall's construction, condition and load path need checking against the proposed pergola and coverings. A convenient fixing location is not evidence that the wall can carry the design. Confirm the responsible design, engineering and approval arrangements before construction, and separate roofing, flashing and weatherproofing from the timber frame in the quote.

Which outdoor timber needs the least upkeep?

Exposure, board profile, finish and drainage influence care as well as species. Compare cleaning and recoating needs for the actual location rather than assuming a timber is maintenance-free.

Second Fix Carpentry Adelaide — Doors, Skirting & Architraves

MEL ONE plans second-fix carpentry around room readiness, floor levels and door schedules. Define the finishing package early so trims, hardware and adjoining trades can meet with fewer unresolved junctions.

Request a second-fix carpentry quote0403 202 949

Second-fix Carpentry and the Finishing Package

Second-fix carpentry brings together ordinary internal doors, skirtings, architraves and agreed timber mouldings once the earlier construction is ready. A useful package identifies rooms, openings, profiles and quantities instead of describing everything as finishing. Timber cornices or curtain-box details can be included where specified; plaster features need their own trade scope.

For a single damaged skirting length or split jamb, a focused repair can be more useful than a whole-room package. Existing stairs also need their purpose considered: a loose decorative trim is different from a moving tread, handrail or barrier. Structural and safety-related stair work needs the relevant assessment and confirmed scope before it is included.

Assess existing stair and barrier repairs

Door and Trim Fit-off: Reveals, Corners and Floor Junctions

The finished floor level, wall thickness and door position determine how the trim meets the room. MEL ONE measures the opening and adjoining junctions before agreeing jamb depth, architrave width, skirting height and corner details. Changed flooring or uneven walls can require different cutting and finishing allowances from those shown on an early plan.

Review visible profiles together, especially at stairs, cabinetry and adjacent openings. A short sample or sound reference length helps explain the intended match when new trim meets old painted material. Confirm any wall correction, filler, caulking or paint work separately so a neat carpentry junction is not confused with a fully finished room.

Repair, replace or install skirting boards · Match architraves and repair door jambs

Door Leaves, Hinges and Hardware Operation

An ordinary internal door needs the right swing, clearances, hinges and latch arrangement as well as an even visible gap. Check the floor finish, nearby cabinetry and the hardware to be supplied before hanging or final adjustment. Where an existing leaf will be reused, assess its condition and fit rather than assuming the old dimensions suit a changed opening.

Fire, acoustic, security or accessibility requirements need specified products and identified professional responsibilities. Ordinary door fitting does not establish the performance of a specialist system. Existing windows, cavity sliders and damaged timber openings can be assessed through the relevant repair service when operation is the main concern.

Second-fix Scheduling Around Other Trades

Linings, moisture conditions, openings and final floor levels need to be sufficiently settled before trim is measured and fixed. Starting while those conditions are still changing can leave incorrect clearances or cause repeat work. Agree room readiness, deliveries and protection with the builder or site contact before booking the finishing stage.
